miniProject.title: Adaptation with checked masks, adapters and teacher signals
miniProject.brief: Extend `lmlab` in `adapt/` with tested full-SFT and LoRA paths, retention controls and a bounded distillation mechanism study. Use the existing model family, lineage and frozen evaluator to decide whether adaptation is worth its training and deployment costs on your machine, without paid teacher APIs.
steps: Prespecify the adaptation question, target and retention slices, matched budgets and stop rules in `registry/`. Plan frozen, prompted and smaller instruction-model baselines against the existing evaluator; independently recount parameters and estimate FLOPs before approving a CPU or single-GPU run plan.

Build the conversation schema and pinned tokenizer/template manifest in `adapt/`. Check train-serve token equality, malformed roles and truncation against template serialization; pass TensorTonic assistant-mask cases, then retain independent shifted-target, stop-token, denominator, accumulation and packed-versus-separate attention-isolation oracles in `tests/`.

Implement counted LoRA factors on the existing decoder using Modern LLM Notebook 16's corrected exercises. Check dense-update forwards and finite-difference gradients before training; retain frozen-base, initialization-gradient, state round-trip, wrong-base rejection and merge/unmerge regressions with declared precision-dependent tolerances.

Build an offline teacher-text manifest with source-group splits, provenance and filter counts. Extend Modern LLM Notebook 17's exercises with full-vocabulary KL-gradient and projected-feature oracles; retain detached teacher, mask and reverse-KL enumeration tests, then a bounded categorical student-prefix update loop with a no-distillation control.

Run bounded full-SFT and LoRA controls only after preflight, checking resumed updates against uninterrupted training. Reconcile post-update tensor-state counts and a context-length memory sweep with measured peaks or CPU storage accounting; retain residual explanations, storage/compute dtype ledgers and a deployment-compatibility decision about quantization.

Compare target-only adaptation with replay at matched total input tokens across seeds, using the frozen `eval/` suite. Retain per-source input and supervised exposure, paired item uncertainty, seed spread and learning-retention plots; investigate regressions against unchanged-model template and parser controls rather than assuming forgetting.

Rebuild a matched quality, retention, training/serving-memory, latency and update-cost table from raw records in a clean process. Include no-training baselines, merged/unmerged adapters, prefill/decode and teacher/filter/rollout costs; retain failed runs and a deployment verdict. Optional common-base task merges require independent arithmetic and behavior regressions.
deliverables: The `adapt/` serializers, full-SFT and LoRA paths, distillation fixtures and independent objective, export and resume tests.
Teacher-data, template, checkpoint and adapter manifests linked to `registry/`, including all failed attempts.
Reproducible learning-retention plots, memory reconciliation and deployment decision with complete training, teacher and inference costs.

checks.name: TensorTonic: Build an Assistant-Only SFT Loss Mask
checks.note: Pass public role-ID cases; add real-template target ownership, denominator, gradient and attention-isolation tests.

checks.name: Modern LLM Notebook 16: parameter count and weight merging
checks.note: Use the corrected factor order from the unit; exercise cells do not replace your decoder-state and gradient regressions.

checks.name: Modern LLM Notebook 17: temperature and hand-KL exercises
checks.note: Extend the named exercises with independent gradients, projected-feature masking and finite-vocabulary reverse-KL enumeration.

rubric.pass: Your template, shifted-mask, denominator and packed-attention oracles pass; dense-update and finite-difference checks validate LoRA before training, with frozen-base, export, wrong-base and resume regressions.
rubric.strong: Injected template shifts, cross-example leakage and duplicate merges fail independently; nonzero adapters preserve logits through serialization and export under justified precision-dependent tolerances.

rubric.pass: Independent KL and projected-feature gradient checks pass; teacher provenance, source-group splits and filtering are recorded, and the detached student-prefix loop retains a matched no-distillation control.
rubric.strong: Exact enumeration distinguishes forward from reverse KL and detached visitation from a full trajectory derivative; teacher errors and unknown provenance explicitly limit the claim.

rubric.pass: Matched full-SFT, LoRA, replay and no-training controls retain seed variation, paired retention, state/peak residuals, dtype compatibility and complete costs; a clean process rebuilds the decision and failures.
rubric.strong: The verdict separates learning from elicitation and retention from exposure, explains when plain LoRA suffices, and distinguishes measured resource savings from estimates and unsupported deployment claims.

miniProject.feedsInto: Versioned SFT checkpoints, adapter exports, masks, teacher-signal oracles and retention slices feed Preference Modeling and Direct Optimization, RL Post-training and Reasoning, multimodal adaptation and the capstone's matched-budget post-training study.
